compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

On 2026-08-12T09:48:03Z the host observability probe published, in a SINGLE run:
  rebar/host:review_interrupts_bound_exceeded      = 7
  rebar/host:review_interrupts_signal_unavailable  = 1

No corresponding events occurred in that interval. Evidence:
  - journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy retention reaches back to 2026-07-03T19:50:40Z (no rotation loss).
  - Full-journal totals at investigation time: bound-exceeded = 8, signal-unavailable = 1.
  - The ONLY signal-unavailable marker in the entire journal is dated 2026-08-04T00:36:41Z — 5.5 days BEFORE it was published as 'new this interval'.
  - Offset files /var/lib/rebar/autodeploy-interrupt-bound-offset and -signal-offset now hold 8 and 1.

## Mechanism

infra/scripts/observability.sh publish_autodeploy_marker_delta() turns a cumulative full-journal
grep -c into a per-interval delta using a persisted offset file:

    total=$(journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy.service --no-pager -o cat | grep -cE "$token")
    prev=$(cat "$offset_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    new=$((total - prev))

When the offset file does not yet exist (a NEWLY INTRODUCED counter), prev defaults to 0, so
new = total = every matching marker in the whole retained journal. The counter's first run
republishes the entire journal history as if it all happened in that one interval.

The function already guards the OPPOSITE direction — 'new < 0' (lost history / rotation) is
clamped to 0 with a documented rationale (bug 2dc7-31b7-ecbb-4cd2, and the rotation double-count
clamp 1648). The cold-start case (offset ABSENT rather than journal SHRUNK) is the complementary
gap and is not guarded at all.

## Why this matters (near-miss)

The two reason-scoped alarms (junco/1650) are 1-datapoint, threshold>0 latches. They were created
at 2026-08-12T11:40:58Z — roughly two hours AFTER the probe's first run at 09:48:03Z. That ordering
is luck. Had terraform applied before the probe shipped (the usual order), BOTH alarms would have
fired immediately from stale history, including
rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-signal-unavailable — the alarm whose own description calls it
'the URGENT one ... the drain check itself is broken, EVERY deploy is running blind' — from a
single, already-resolved 2026-08-04 event. That is a false page against a pristine system.

This is a FALSE-POSITIVE-generating defect in metric emission, not an alarm-threshold problem: the
alarms are correct to fire on a nonzero count; the count itself was fabricated. The bug is latent
and will recur on every future new counter added to this shared helper, and on any offset-file loss
(fresh /var/lib/rebar, host rebuild, disk restore).

## Scope

publish_autodeploy_marker_delta is the shared helper for deploy_deferrals, review_interrupts,
review_interrupts_bound_exceeded, review_interrupts_signal_unavailable. The same
cumulative-minus-offset shape (with the same cold-start gap) is duplicated in observability.sh §3
(replication_errors), §4 (voter_errors), and §4b (g2p_dispatch_errors). Those counters' offset
files already exist, so they are not currently mis-emitting — but they carry the identical defect
on offset loss or host rebuild.

## Suggested fix direction (not prescriptive)

Seed the offset on cold start instead of publishing history: when the offset file is absent, write
total to it and publish 0 for that run. Optionally record a one-line 'counter initialised at N'
log so the seeding is auditable. Applying it inside the shared helper covers all four autodeploy
counters at once; the three open-coded copies should get the same treatment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the offset file absent and a journal containing N matching markers, the counter publishes 0 (not N) and seeds the offset to N. Verify: unit/integration test over publish_autodeploy_marker_delta covering the absent-offset case.
- [ ] A marker emitted AFTER the seeding run still publishes 1 on the next run (seeding must not swallow genuinely new events).
- [ ] The existing negative-delta (lost-history) clamp behaviour is preserved and still covered by its test.
- [ ] The open-coded counters in §3 (replication_errors), §4 (voter_errors) and §4b (g2p_dispatch_errors) either share the fixed helper or apply the same cold-start seeding.

## Verification

Discovered by ops sweep of AWS alarm firings since 2026-08-12T04:00Z; full evidence trail recorded
as a comment on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet (b902-18af-14ed-4da1). All investigation was read-only
(CloudWatch describe/get + SSM read-only journalctl); nothing in AWS or on the box was mutated.
## Implementation plan (current main 3c1972e9c0)

Mirror bug 1648 (change `34759270dd`): a minimal bash delta at every offset site, one full
rationale comment at §3 and one-line back-references elsewhere.

### Change — infra/scripts/observability.sh (6 sites)

Each site today reads:

    prev=$(cat "$OFFSET" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    case "$prev" in '' | *[!0-9]*) prev=0 ;; esac

An ABSENT file yields the literal `0` from the `|| echo 0` fallback, so `new = total - 0` =
the whole retained journal. Replace the fallback with a cold-start seed:

    prev=$(cat "$OFFSET" 2>/dev/null || true)
    case "$prev" in '' | *[!0-9]*) prev=$total ;; esac

`prev=$total` makes `new=0` for that run, and the existing publish-then-persist block writes
`$total` to the offset, so the counter starts measuring from the next interval. An empty or
non-numeric offset takes the same branch: an unreadable offset is indistinguishable from none,
and the fabrication risk is identical. A file holding a real `0` still parses as 0 (unchanged).

Sites (line numbers on 3c1972e9c0):
- 101-102 §3 `replication_errors` (`REPL_OFFSET_FILE`) — carries the full rationale comment
- 142-143 §4 `voter_errors`
- 167-168 §4c `review_bot_merge_change_errors`
- 190-191 §4d `deploy_errors`
- 242-243 `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta()` — covers deploy_deferrals, review_interrupts,
  review_interrupts_bound_exceeded, review_interrupts_signal_unavailable
- 302-303 §4b `g2p_dispatch_errors`

Invariant, stated once at §3 and referenced at the rest: no offset means this counter has never
observed the source, so every marker in the journal predates monitoring by it — the cold-start
complement of 1648's "lost history is already-counted". Under-counts at most the markers emitted
inside the single initialising interval; self-heals in one run.

### Tests — tests/scripts/test_observability_coldstart_e2a6.py

New file mirroring `test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py` (same stub harness: curl/git/logger/
journalctl/aws stubs, `_values()` reader, the seven-target parametrisation).

1. `test_cold_start_publishes_zero_and_seeds_the_offset` — parametrised over all seven metrics:
   offset files ABSENT, journal populated with N markers -> published value is `[0]` and the
   offset file now holds `N`.
2. `test_markers_after_initialisation_still_publish` — the journalctl stub reads its marker count
   from a file, so run 1 initialises at N and run 2 (N+1 markers) publishes `1`. Seeding is not
   sticky.
3. Regression: `test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py` and `test_observability_offsets_6a65.py` must
   still pass unchanged (negative-delta clamp and publish-then-persist preserved).

RED-verified against unfixed main first (expect N, get 0).

### Deploy

No manual box action: autodeploy.sh watches `OBS_PATHS` and re-runs install-observability.sh on a
probe-source change (as 1648 noted).

### Out of scope

Alarm thresholds/definitions (they are correct); the offset-file storage location; any change to
the negative-delta clamp.

file_impact.reason: publish_autodeploy_marker_delta() and the open-coded counters in sections 3, 4 and 4b treat an absent offset file as prev=0 and republish the entire retained journal as one interval delta; the cold-start seeding fix lands here

compiled_state.title: observability.sh marker-delta counters republish ALL journal history on cold start (absent offset file), producing false alarm firings
